description: Patient Priya Sundaram presented with acute retrosternal chest discomfort and burning sensation. Admitted to rule out acute coronary syndrome. Serial high-sensitivity Troponin-I at 0, 3, and 6 hours returned strictly negative (<0.01 ng/mL). 12-lead ECG demonstrated normal sinus rhythm without ischemic ST-T changes. Upper GI evaluation revealed marked gastroesophageal reflux. Final clinical diagnosis: Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis (K21.9). Acute myocardial infarction (I21.9) was definitively ruled out. Patient symptomatically relieved with intravenous pantoprazole.
